page: Microsoft Azure E16bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions. It is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual core.

The E16bs_v5 instance contains no bundled local disk storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on remote managed block storage attachments, with platform architecture optimized specifically for high-throughput Azure Premium Storage disks. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent median-tier computational and memory throughput across industry tests. The instance records a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 1670.0 and a multi-core score of 10077.0, matching average tier performance in PassMark CPU tests at 21286.76. Uncached system memory bandwidth achieves 100.1 GB/sec for sequential reads and 59.98 GB/sec for writes, scaling to 834.28 GB/sec in cached small-block scenarios. Synthetic database evaluation records 7985.51 PassMark database operations and 15.81 million Redis SET operations per second, while lightweight LLM text generation on a 135M model reaches 268.04 tokens per second.

Resource allocation focuses on high RAM density and remote storage bandwidth efficiency rather than raw compute scaling or local ephemeral NVMe disks. The absence of local scratch disks requires external storage planning for high-IOPS applications. The instance profile is suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise ERP deployments, medium-scale data analysis, and memory-constrained static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E16bs_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of system RAM. Utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside an L3 cache of 48 MB and AVX-512 vector acceleration. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or graphics acceleration hardware, requiring external network-attached block volumes for persistence. Benchmark evaluations place the instance consistently within the middle performance quartile across compute and memory workloads, reaching 100.1 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 15.81 million Redis SET operations per second, and a PassMark CPU score of 21286.76. The instance is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads including relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and analytics backends.
